# Review — iliad-046 (8.1–96)

Two passes. Pass 1 checked, in order: every grammatical label, every claim about where a word stands and every cross-reference in every note against the line and the repository; Greek → `l` word by word; `l` ↔ `i`; remembered English in `i`; quotation marks and `mark`; then the mechanics (tiling, `p`, `ln`, line counts, apostrophes and backticks, note length). Pass 2 re-read the whole edited file from the top, re-ran the tiling and quotation checks, re-ran the validator's repeated-Greek test (section 6 and 6b) by hand against the published parts, and re-checked every changed unit. `gloss.json` does not exist yet, so the second pass could not check parses against it; that check belongs to whoever runs the gloss pass. All edits were made to `units.json` by script; `t` was never edited. One edit (the join of 8.81–82 with 8.83–84) changes where a unit begins and ends; the text of the part is unchanged (the units' `t` joined in order is byte-identical before and after, checked by script), and it is explained in the first table row below. `units.json` went from 71 to 70 units.

## Verified before editing

- Tiling, as the build checks it: the units reproduce the 96 lines; `ln` correct on every unit; `p` on exactly the eight ¶ lines (1, 28, 38, 41, 53, 60, 66, 78); `l` has one `\n` per `\n` in `t`; no `\n` in `i`; no ASCII apostrophe or backtick anywhere in `units.json`. One failure, below (8.81–82 ended with no punctuation).
- Scansion: the packet flags none. The scanner reports "spondaic fifth" on lines 3, 12, 25, 27, 31, 33, 54, 55, none AMBIGUOUS or UNRESOLVED. Scanned by hand: each has a spondee in the fifth foot closing on a polysyllable (Οὐλύμποιο, Οὔλυμπον δέ, ἀνθρώπων, κρειόντων, αἰχμητάων, θωρήσσοντο, ὁπλίζοντο), which is a regular, if uncommon, hexameter; line 3 is the same line as 1.499 and 5.754. No irregularity, so no note.
- Recurrences, grepped in the pinned source (`source/iliad-monro-allen1920.json`, `../odyssey/source/odyssey-murray1919.json`) and the published parts: 8.58–59 = 2.809–810 (and 8.59 = Od 24.70); 8.60–65 = 4.446–451, line for line; 8.71 = 3.127, 3.131 and 3.251 (a whole line, not a half-line); 8.45 = Od 3.484 (the whole line also at Il 5.366 and Od 3.494; its first half-line also at Od 6.82 and 15.192); 8.82 = 3.329 and 7.355; 8.31 = Od 1.45, 1.81, 24.473; 8.3 = 1.499 and 5.754; 8.66 = Od 9.56 and Il 11.84; 8.93 = 2.173, 4.358, 9.308 etc. and Od 5.203 etc. All the drafter's claims hold. The published English for the whole units that repeat (8.45b–46, 8.59b, 8.60–62, 8.62b–63, 8.64–65) is carried over exactly; by my run of the validator's test, those five units match and nothing differs.
- Later repeats noted for the owner (not defects): 8.5 = 19.101; 8.33 = 8.464; 8.39–40 = 22.183–184; 8.41–44 = 13.23–26; 8.69–70 = 22.209–210. Whoever drafts those parts takes this part's English.
- Speech framing: the previous part (`/home/user/Lectorium/iliad-045.json`) ends at 7.482 with the book's last line, "They lay down to sleep…", no speech open; 8.1 therefore opens plain. Speeches here: Zeus 5–27, Athena 31–37, Zeus 39–40, Diomedes 93–96. Each opens with “ on the first unit and closes with ” on the last, and `mark` sits on the first unit of each (Zeus speaks, Athena speaks, Zeus answers, Diomedes speaks). Opening and closing marks: 4 and 4 in `l`, 4 and 4 in `i` after the fix below. Diomedes' speech does not run on into the next part: see the first row.

## The 8.59b / 8.63 clash — decided: left

The half-line πολὺς δ’ ὀρυμαγδὸς ὀρώρει has "and a great din had risen." / "rose" at 8.59 and "had sprung up" / "went up" at 8.63. Each stands in a whole unit whose Greek has already been published (iliad-015 and odyssey-115 for the short unit; iliad-025 for 8.62b–63), and the validator (section 6) fails any unit whose letters match an earlier published unit but whose English differs. So neither can be changed without breaking the gate, and no published part may be touched from here. The unit notes at 8.59 and 8.62 say that the other wording exists. The deeper inconsistency is old: the conventions row for 2.810 gives "had sprung up" / "went up", while the shipped iliad-015 reads "had risen" / "rose". That is the owner's to harmonise (one republish of iliad-015 or of iliad-025 and odyssey-115).

## Findings considered and refused

- Units that end at a comma where the sentence is only two or three lines (8.1, 8.7, 8.36, 8.47, 8.49, 8.53, 8.56, 8.66, 8.68, 8.70, 8.85): the Odyssey rule is "never at a comma unless a period would run past four lines". The build accepts a comma ending, the cure is joining units (editing `t`), and only the one build-blocking case was joined. Left, and flagged for the owner as a segmentation point; the English of every one of them is complete and reads on.
- 8.50 ἠέρα πουλύν "a thick mist": the published 5.776 has "much mist" / "a great mist" for the same phrase. The table's ἠέρι πολλῇ (3.381) and the Odyssey's ἠέρα (7.15) both read "thick mist", so "thick" has two house rows to one published outlier, which cannot be touched here. Left; the row cites the table.
- 8.54 ῥίμφα "nimbly": the Iliad row for 6.511 has "lightly" and lists "nimbly" as avoided, but the Odyssey table (12.182, 13.83, binding) has "nimbly" and ships it for fast motion; "lightly" is used of a horse's knees. A judgement call; left, with the drafter's row recording it.
- 8.7 the added "And" in `l` and `i` ("And let no female god"): it carries the continuative force of the paired μήτε … μήτε. Left.
- 8.10 "struck down" for πληγείς: the sense (he comes back to Olympus) is clear from the clause; no stronger than "struck". Left.
- 8.4 the note's "ὑπό suggesting the hearer below the speaker": an interpretation, labelled as what the literal layer shows. Left.
- 8.21 "would never drag" for οὐκ ἂν ἐρύσαιτ’ … οὐδ’ εἰ: "never" is the force of the potential with οὐδ’ εἰ; `l` has the plain "would not". Left.
- 8.39–40 "my heart is not wholly in what I say" against `l` "not at all, you see, with a ready-minded heart do I speak": the `i` gives the sense and the note says so; "not at all" in the Greek belongs to the idiom, not to Zeus's real intent, which the next clause (kindness) makes plain. Left.
- 8.69 "the Father" (capital) in `i` against "the father" in `l`: the capital is the plain English sign of a title standing for a name, and the note names Zeus. Left.
- 8.28 ἀγασσάμενοι "in admiration": the sense "wonder at" is arguably nearer cowed awe, but the house sets "in admiration at" for 7.404 and the note records the two senses. Left.
- 8.58 and 8.67 λαός as "people" in `l` and "army" / "troops" in `i`: the same pairing as the published 2.809–810 (only the "troops" at 8.67 was changed, to "army"). Left.
- 8.31 `l`/`i` carry no commas that the Odyssey line has (the edition prints none): the English is the Odyssey's, as in the packet. Left.
- 8.43 ἑοῦ "his own" lost in `i`: `l` has it, the note says it. Left.
- 8.39 the mark "Zeus answers" for a speech that follows a speech by Athena: the model's marks are "X speaks"; "answers" is the Odyssey's. Left.
